Adding Custom Patient-Level Prediction Algorithms

Jenna Reps, Martijn J. Schuemie, Patrick B. Ryan, Peter R. Rijnbeek

2026-11-13

Source: vignettes/AddingCustomModels.Rmd
AddingCustomModels.Rmd

Introduction

This vignette describes how you can add your own custom algorithms in the Observational Health Data Sciences and Informatics (OHDSI) PatientLevelPrediction package. This allows you to fully leverage the OHDSI PatientLevelPrediction framework for model development and validation. This vignette assumes you have read and are comfortable with building single patient level prediction models as described in the vignette('BuildingPredictiveModels').

We invite you to share your new algorithms with the OHDSI community through our GitHub repository.

Algorithm Code Structure

A model is described by a set<Name> function that returns its modelSettings. PatientLevelPrediction does the rest: fitClassifier() prepares the data, runs the hyperparameter search with cross-validation, fits the final model and builds the plpModel, and predictPlp(), savePlpModel() and loadPlpModel() use the same settings later. The model itself supplies a few functions, the hooks, which are named in its settings. The xgboost model in GradientBoostingMachine.R is a complete example.

Set

The set<Name> function takes the hyperparameter values to search and returns a list of class modelSettings with:

  • param - a named list of hyperparameter values; createHyperparameterSettings() decides how candidates are drawn from them (a grid by default)
  • settings - the model’s settings and its hooks:
    • modelName, modelType ("binary") and seed
    • prepareData - turns the training data into what train expects, usually "toSparseM" (a sparse matrix with one row per patient). If it has a settings argument, it also gets these settings.
    • train - fits the model for one set of hyperparameters
    • predict - predicts risks with a fitted model
    • variableImportance - gives the importance of each covariate
    • saveType - how the fitted model is saved: the name of a save handler (see below), "RtoJson" for a model that is an R list, or "file" for a model that is a folder of files

Each hook can be a function, the name of a function, or "pkg::function". A name is looked up in PatientLevelPrediction and then on the search path, so plain names are meant for the package’s own functions; "pkg::function" is an exported function of an installed package, which is loaded but does not need to be attached. Use the "pkg::function" form for hooks in your own package, so that saved models still work in a new R session. All hooks are looked up before fitting starts, so a misspelled one fails at once.

For example, a model called madeUp with two hyperparameters:

setMadeUp <- function(a = c(1, 4, 10), b = 2, seed = NULL) {
  # add input checks here...
  if (is.null(seed)) {
    seed <- sample(100000, 1)
  }

  param <- list(
    a = a,
    b = b
  )

  settings <- list(
    modelName = "Made Up",
    modelType = "binary",
    seed = seed,
    prepareData = "toSparseM",
    train = "myPackage::fitMadeUp",
    predict = "myPackage::predictMadeUp",
    variableImportance = "myPackage::varImpMadeUp",
    saveType = "myPackage::saveLoadMadeUp"
  )

  result <- list(
    param = param,
    settings = settings
  )
  class(result) <- "modelSettings"

  return(result)
}

Train

The train hook fits the model for one candidate. It gets:

  • dataMatrix - the prepared data, a sparse matrix with rows as patients and columns as features when prepareData is "toSparseM"
  • labels - a data.frame where labels$outcomeCount is the class label (0 or 1) per patient
  • hyperParameters - a named list with one value per hyperparameter
  • settings - the settings from the set function, such as the seed

and returns the fitted model.

fitMadeUp <- function(dataMatrix, labels, hyperParameters, settings) {
  # set the seed for reproducibility
  set.seed(settings$seed)

  model <- madeUpModel(
    X = dataMatrix,
    Y = labels$outcomeCount,
    a = hyperParameters$a,
    b = hyperParameters$b
  )

  return(model)
}

An error in train or predict stops the search, so that problems in the model’s code show up at once. When the model knows that a candidate simply cannot be fitted, for example because it runs out of memory, it can call stopCandidate() instead. The search then warns, records the candidate with a missing performance and the message, and goes on with the next one; it stops only if every candidate is skipped.

fitMadeUp <- function(dataMatrix, labels, hyperParameters, settings) {
  model <- tryCatch(
    madeUpModel(X = dataMatrix, Y = labels$outcomeCount, a = hyperParameters$a),
    madeUpOutOfMemory = function(e) stopCandidate("out of memory")
  )
  return(model)
}

Predict

The predict hook gets:

  • plpModel - during the search the model returned by train, and after fitting the plpModel
  • data - during the search a part of the prepared data, and when predicting on new data a plpData object
  • cohort - the patients to predict for

It returns the cohort with a column value holding the predicted risks. The rows must keep the original rowIds: toSparseM() numbers the matrix rows and keeps the original in originalRowId.

predictMadeUp <- function(plpModel, data, cohort) {
  if (inherits(data, "plpData")) {
    matrixObjects <- toSparseM(
      plpData = data,
      cohort = cohort,
      map = plpModel$covariateImportance %>%
        dplyr::select("columnId", "covariateId")
    )
    newData <- matrixObjects$dataMatrix
    cohort <- matrixObjects$labels
  } else {
    newData <- data
  }

  if (inherits(plpModel, "plpModel")) {
    model <- plpModel$model
  } else {
    model <- plpModel
  }

  prediction <- cohort
  prediction$value <- stats::predict(model, newData)

  # give back the original rowIds
  prediction <- prediction %>%
    dplyr::select(-"rowId") %>%
    dplyr::rename(rowId = "originalRowId")

  attr(prediction, "metaData") <- list(modelType = attr(plpModel, "modelType"))
  return(prediction)
}

As the madeUp model uses the standard R prediction, it could reuse xgboost’s prediction function instead: predict = "PatientLevelPrediction::predictXgboost".

Variable importance

The variableImportance hook gets the fitted model and a data.frame called covariateMap with the covariateId and columnId of each column of the feature matrix. It returns a data.frame with the columns covariateId, covariateValue (the importance) and included (1 if the model uses the covariate, otherwise 0). If it fails, the model is still fitted, without importances.

varImpMadeUp <- function(model, covariateMap) {
  covariateMap$covariateValue <- madeUpImportance(model)[covariateMap$columnId]
  covariateMap$included <- as.numeric(covariateMap$covariateValue != 0)
  return(covariateMap[, c("covariateId", "covariateValue", "included")])
}

Saving and loading

A save handler is a function that returns a list with:

  • save - a function of the fitted model and a file path that writes the model
  • load - a function of a file path that reads it back
  • fileName - optionally, the name of the file (or folder) to write in the model folder, a plain name without a path; the default is "model.json" 
saveLoadMadeUp <- function() {
  list(
    fileName = "model.rds",
    save = function(model, file) saveRDS(model, file),
    load = function(file) readRDS(file)
  )
}

savePlpModel() calls save with file.path(modelFolder, fileName) and loadPlpModel() calls load with the same path.
